item.title: Nitin's 'Nabin' team: BJP hits reset button with eye on UP and 'Mission 2029'
item.description: The Bharatiya Janata Party has unveiled its dynamic new national team of office-bearers, strategically assembled to tackle both the upcoming assembly elections and the 2029 Lok Sabha contest. This diverse lineup features a mix of seasoned politicians and fresh talent, representing various regions. Some notable figures are making returns, while others have been sidelined, highlighting the party's commitment to revitalizing its organizational framework for future challenges.

item.title: BWF Worlds: Ayush Shetty stuns World No. 1 Shi Yu Qi; India 5-0 on Day 1
item.description: Ayush Shetty produced the biggest win of his career on Day 1 at the BWF World Championships, stunning top seed and defending champion Shi Yu Qi in a thrilling contest. Led by the young Indian's heroics and PV Sindhu's comfortable win, India made a perfect 5-0 start on the opening day of the tournament in New Delhi.
item.dc:creator: TANUJ LAKHINA

item.title: 100 days of TVK govt: CM Vijay defines priorities, but his real test begins now
item.description: Tamil Nadu's new Chief Minister Vijay's government has completed its first hundred days. The administration has focused heavily on welfare programs and social initiatives. Significant investment commitments have also been secured for the state's development. The government has implemented measures to address women's safety and curb drug use. But now delivery of these promises will be closely watched.
item.dc:creator: PRIYANKA MUKHERJEE

item.title: US student wins award for geometry breakthrough: How it can change modern medicine
item.description: Connor Hill won first place at the 2026 Regeneron Science Talent Search competition. His research classified noble polyhedra, identifying two infinite families and 146 isolated examples. Hill translated a geometric problem into a finite algebraic one for a complete classification. This method of reducing complexity is vital for modern biology and drug discovery. His work demonstrates how mathematical simplification aids understanding in complex scientific fields.

item.title: ‘Show composure’: Coach’s message to India ahead of must-not-lose Pakistan clash
item.description: Following India's defeat in the Hockey World Cup, coach Craig Fulton emphasised the necessity for stricter defensive discipline. He urged players to maintain composure and enhance their defensive strategies ahead of the critical match against Pakistan. Midfielder Manpreet Singh echoed his sentiments, pinpointing defensive errors as pivotal to their loss. A point against Pakistan is essential for India's progression to the next round.

item.title: MacKenzie Scott helped abolish $40bn in medical debt; how mechanics work
item.description: MacKenzie Scott's philanthropic efforts have made a significant impact by enabling the cancellation of medical debt across the United States. By purchasing and eliminating patient debt at a minimal cost, she has set a precedent that encourages other wealthy individuals to invest in similar initiatives. Despite these immediate acts of generosity, the need for comprehensive policy reforms persists, as true transformation necessitates addressing the fundamental issues leading to medical debt.

item.title: Meet Ananya Nagendra, 18, who built an ant-based digester for food waste
item.description: A student developed an ant-based digester to process food waste efficiently. This innovative system uses ants to break down organic materials, reducing landfill methane. Experiments showed Camponotus castaneus ants consumed the most waste, proving effective. Her prototype achieved an impressive eighty-three percent efficiency in initial tests. This research offers a novel biological approach to managing discarded food materials.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Nebraska bridge heats itself from inside to melt snow during storms
item.description: A Nebraska bridge is using 52 slabs of conductive concrete that can heat its surface and melt snow and ice during winter storms. Developed by University of Nebraska-Lincoln professor Chris Tuan, the technology uses steel shavings and carbon particles to carry electricity through the concrete. The system could reduce the need for de-icing chemicals at bridges, airport tarmacs, intersections and other icy areas.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Accenture CEO Julie Sweet makes a 'vacation request' to employees for this month
item.description: Accenture's CEO, Julie Sweet, has requested that employees delay their vacation in August. This temporary policy adjustment is designed to bolster staff presence as the company approaches the end of its financial year. Following disappointing quarterly results and a forecasted drop in revenue, Accenture is permitting employees to carry over unused vacation days into the next fiscal year to help enhance fourth-quarter outputs and revenue generation.
item.dc:creator: TIMESOFINDIA.COM

item.title: ‘Pollution is pretty insane’: Antonsen wants India Open to move out of Delhi winter
item.description: Danish badminton player Anders Antonsen has voiced concerns regarding the BWF's scheduling of the India Open, criticising the January-February timeframe due to the heavy winter pollution in Delhi. He chose to miss this year's tournament, incurring a fine as a result. Antonsen believes that the winter air quality severely hampers athletes' performance and calls for improved conditions in future competitions.

item.description: Andretti driver Jake Dennis lost the Formula E World Championship to Porsche’s Pascal Wehrlein after a disappointing London E-Prix. However, his fiancee Lexi Grace Boosey and several Formula E drivers praised him for how he performed throughout the season and finished second in the championship.

item.title: 'I've cried for a long time': Taylor Barnard breaks down after historic Formula E win
item.description: Taylor Barnard made Formula E history with a dramatic first win at the London E-Prix on Sunday. The 22-year-old DS PENSKE driver became the youngest race winner in the championship after passing Nyck de Vries with two laps left. The victory came in front of his home crowd and family, leaving Barnard emotional after a difficult season and a long wait for success.

item.title: 'Let me die in peace right now': Chargesheet reveals Twisha's chilling final message
item.description: The CBI's chargesheet highlights the alleged cruelty faced by Twisha Sharma at the hands of her husband and mother-in-law, who reportedly inflicted mental and psychological torment during their union. Notably, Twisha communicated a final message to her sister-in-law shortly before her passing. The post-mortem revealed that her demise resulted from suicide via ante-mortem hanging, with investigations ongoing as forensic data from devices and CCTV footage is awaited.

item.title: WC: India coach questions FIH over China’s penalty stroke, later deletes posts
item.description: Indian women's hockey coach questioned the penalty-stroke rule interpretation after a draw. He shared footage and sought clarification from the International Hockey Federation. Former players also expressed their views on the controversial penalty-stroke action. The coach later removed his social media posts regarding the incident. FIH had not responded to clarification requests at the time of publication.

item.description: The 2026 BWF World Championships highlight badminton’s global reach, with top representation from Asian powerhouses and Denmark. While nations like Bulgaria, Uganda, and South Africa have fewer athletes and limited resources, their stories underscore dedication and growth.

item.title: House rent in most EU capitals exceed minimum wage
item.description: In numerous EU capitals, rent prices outstrip the minimum wage, significantly impacting low-income earners. Cities like Prague and Lisbon record the highest rent-to-income ratios, especially for two-bedroom apartments. Other capitals also indicate rental costs above the gross monthly minimum wage. However, Brussels and Berlin provide relatively affordable housing options for those earning minimum wage. The escalating housing expenses continue to be a critical issue for workers across Europe.
item.dc:creator: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK

item.title: Hockey WC: India’s 32-year England jinx continues as late goals seal 2-4 defeat
item.description: England secured a 4-2 victory over India in their Hockey World Cup Pool D match. India led 2-1 at halftime after goals from Harmanpreet and Dilpreet Singh. England responded strongly in the second half, scoring three times to seal the win. This defeat means India must draw against Pakistan to advance. The result extends India's winless streak against England in the World Cup.

item.description: Ravindra Jadeja's relentless consistency and Suthar's wrist and finger magic combined to give India a glimpse of a potent left-arm spin partnership in Galle. With seven wickets between them, the duo offered India a template that bridges the present and the future.

item.title: ONGC gets US licence to expand Venezuela operations, boost oil output
item.description: ONGC has successfully obtained approval from the US Treasury, allowing it to further extend its oil operations in Venezuela. The newly acquired license significantly reduces sanctions-related barriers, paving the way for increased investments and production capabilities. With this development, ONGC can explore new contracts and possibly take over projects from PDVSA.

item.title: ‘Jana Nayagan’ OTT: When and where to watch Vijay’s final film
item.description: Jana Nayagan, the much-anticipated final film of Vijay, is set to premiere on Zee5 starting August 21. This political action drama has garnered a varied reception but has enjoyed strong box office success. item.title: Smriti Irani's big comeback: Why BJP has turned to its 'giant killer'
item.description: Smriti Irani is reappointed as a general secretary for the BJP's national team, a move that highlights the party's strategic push in Uttar Pradesh ahead of upcoming elections. Following setbacks in the recent Lok Sabha elections, her previous success in Amethi positions her as a critical asset. This role will see her coordinating with state units and overseeing candidate selections.

item.title: Zoya Akhtar confirms 'Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara 2' with Hrithik, Farhan and Abhay
item.description: Zoya Akhtar confirmed 'Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara 2' is in development with Reema Kagti, though its future remains uncertain until the right story emerges. A 2025 ad reignited fan buzz. Zoya also dismissed criticism about her films focusing on privileged characters, defending her creative freedom to tell varied stories.

item.title: No new strikes, no peace deal: What Donald Trump’s ‘low-key’ Iran strategy means
item.description: The United States is employing a low-key strategy against Iran after a deadline expired. Economic pressure and diplomacy are now the primary tools being utilized. The US is maintaining sanctions and a naval blockade to influence Tehran. This approach aims to avoid immediate military escalation while seeking concessions. Backchannel communications continue as both sides assess their leverage.

item.description: During a recent meeting in Goa, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge passionately led a rendition of Vande Mataram, addressing BJP workers who protested against his convoy, alleging disrespect. In response, Kharge challenged the BJP's claims about patriotism, reminding attendees of the party's historical connections to the British Empire. This demonstration came amidst a new directive from the Union home ministry regarding the proper performance of the national song.

item.title: DU suspends PhD scholar for slapping professor, bars campus entry; CCTV video emerges
item.description: Delhi University has taken decisive action by suspending a PhD scholar from its law faculty. Following allegations of an assault on a professor earlier this week, the scholar has also been prohibited from entering university premises effective immediately. The incident, which was captured on CCTV showing the scholar slapping the professor, will now be investigated by an independent committee to ensure accountability and transparency.

item.title: Kangana Ranaut on 'Bharat Bhagya Vidhaata': 'Patriotism has many forms'
item.description: Kangana Ranaut discussed 'Bharat Bhagya Vidhaata', saying patriotism extends beyond soldiers to doctors, nurses and ordinary citizens who act with courage. She hopes the film teaches younger generations that heroism exists in everyday choices, not just grand moments. The film, directed by Manoj Tapadia, is now streaming on Zee5.

item.title: Shabnam Sinha to succeed Sunil Bharti Mittal as Airtel Payments Bank chairperson
item.description: Shabnam Sinha is set to take over as chairperson of Airtel Payments Bank starting October 1. With Sunil Bharti Mittal concluding his term as non-executive chairman on September 30, 2026, Sinha's appointment is timely. As an independent director with profound leadership credentials, she intends to leverage the bank's substantial growth and enhance digital banking access throughout India, reinforcing its commitment to innovation and expansion.
item.dc:creator: SAURABH SINHA

item.title: Jadeja scripts history with 350th wicket, joins Kapil, Botham, Vettori in elite club
item.description: Ravindra Jadeja achieved a significant career milestone in Test cricket. He became the fourth player ever to score 4,000 runs and take 350 wickets. This remarkable feat was accomplished during the first Test against Sri Lanka. Jadeja joins an elite group of all-rounders with this achievement. His efficiency is highlighted by reaching this landmark in under 100 matches.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: Once plagued by elephant raids, Assam village now grows grass & fruits for wild herds
item.description: In Hatikhuli-Ronghang village, a remarkable relationship with wild elephant herds has blossomed. By establishing dedicated feeding zones, the community effectively reduces crop damage and tackles food shortages along traditional elephant migration routes. This transformation has allowed farmers to resume paddy cultivation, fostering a newfound harmony between humans and elephants. The Hati Bondhu initiative beautifully illustrates the potential for peaceful coexistence between culture and wildlife.
item.dc:creator: PRIYA SRIVASTAVA
